pointers.sentence: A cached page's key hashes the values of the request headers that its response's `"Vary"` names, all but Accept-Language while `USE_I18N` is true (`django/utils/cache.py:learn_cache_key`), and a fragment's key, made by `make_template_fragment_key` for the `{% cache %}` tag, hashes the values it varies on.

Since 6.1 each value goes into the hash as a netstring: its length in bytes, a colon, the bytes and a comma (`django/utils/cache.py:_generate_cache_key`, `django/core/cache/utils.py:make_template_fragment_key`).

Django's tests check the headers `"EU"` then nothing against nothing then `"EU"`, and the fragment's values `"a:b"` then `"c"` against `"a"` then `"b:c"` (`tests/cache/tests.py:CacheUtils.test_learn_cache_key_no_header_collision`, `tests/cache/tests.py:TestMakeTemplateFragmentKey.test_collision_vary_on`).

The release notes give the cost: after the upgrade, the first request for a page or fragment stored so is a miss (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`).

`DatabaseCache.get_many`, which `DatabaseCache.get` calls, has decoded each unexpired value with strict Base64 since 6.1, so a value with a character outside the alphabet raises `binascii.Error` where, in the release notes' words, it was silently ignored (`django/core/cache/backends/db.py:DatabaseCache.get_many`).

Now a write counts and culls only when a random draw is at most `"CULL_PROBABILITY"` of the alias's `"OPTIONS"`, an optimisation in the release notes' words (`django/core/cache/backends/db.py:DatabaseCache._base_set`).

`BaseDatabaseCache.__init__` reads the option: 0.1 when it is absent or `float` refuses it, and 0 turns culling off (`django/core/cache/backends/db.py:BaseDatabaseCache.__init__`; [The cache backends](../services/cache-backends.md)).

`File.open` gives the arguments after the mode to the built-in `open` since 5.0, when it reopens a closed file whose name is a path that exists; a file still open is only rewound (`django/core/files/base.py:File.open`).

With `allow_overwrite=True`, `FileSystemStorage._save` opens the content it streams with `os.O_TRUNC` in place of `os.O_EXCL` and moves a temporary file over an existing one (`django/core/files/move.py:file_move_safe`), `FileSystemStorage.is_name_available` looks only at the length, and `FileSystemStorage.get_alternative_name` returns the name unchanged, so a file saved under a taken name replaces the one there (`django/core/files/storage/filesystem.py:FileSystemStorage._save`; [File storage: `Storage`, `FileSystemStorage` and `storages`](../services/storage.md)).

The default storages come from `STORAGES` alone: `default_storage` stands for its `"default"` alias and `staticfiles_storage` for its `"staticfiles"` alias (`django/core/files/storage/__init__.py:DefaultStorage`, `django/contrib/staticfiles/storage.py:ConfiguredStorage`).

`Signal.send` calls the synchronous receivers in order and then runs the coroutine functions through one `async_to_sync`; `Signal.asend` and `Signal.asend_robust`, new in 5.0, run the synchronous receivers through one `sync_to_async` and then the coroutine functions on the caller's loop (`django/dispatch/dispatcher.py:Signal.send`, `django/dispatch/dispatcher.py:Signal.asend`; [Signals: `Signal`, receivers and sending](../services/signals.md)).

Since 6.1 the coroutine receivers of one send run as tasks of one `asyncio.TaskGroup`, where they used to be run with asyncio's gather (`django/dispatch/dispatcher.py:_run_parallel`; `docs/topics/signals.txt`).

The deserializers of the Python, JSON, JSON Lines and YAML formats have been classes since 5.2, where they were functions, for extensibility in a project's own formats, the release notes say (`docs/releases/5.2.txt`).

The last three subclass the Python format's `Deserializer` and hand it their parsed text; it builds each object in `_handle_object`, calling `_handle_fk_field_node`, `_handle_m2m_field_node` and `_get_model_from_node`, which a subclass may override (`django/core/serializers/python.py:Deserializer`).
The JSON serializer's output has ended in a newline since 6.0, indented or not (`django/core/serializers/json.py:Serializer.end_serialization`).

Since 6.2 `DjangoJSONEncoder` writes a datetime or a time to the millisecond only when its milliseconds are not zero, and otherwise to the second; the release notes' example, a datetime with one microsecond, was written with `".000"` before (`django/core/serializers/json.py:DjangoJSONEncoder.default`).

A `natural_key` that returns an empty tuple counts as none since 6.1: under `use_natural_primary_keys=True` the object is written with its primary key, and under `use_natural_foreign_keys=True` a relation to it as it is written without natural keys (`django/core/serializers/python.py:Serializer.get_dump_object`, `django/core/serializers/python.py:Serializer.handle_fk_field`, `django/core/serializers/python.py:Serializer.handle_m2m_field`).

The XML deserializer raises `SuspiciousOperation` since 6.1 when a field's text holds an element with content of its own, and passes over an empty one (`django/core/serializers/xml_serializer.py:check_element_type`).

`DeserializedObject.save` has set each many-to-many relation with `raw=True` since 6.1, so the relations loaddata sets send `m2m_changed` with raw true, as `pre_save` and `post_save` already were (`django/core/serializers/base.py:DeserializedObject.save`; [Fixtures: dumpdata and loaddata](../services/fixtures.md)).

A paginator has taken `error_messages=` since 5.0, merged by key over `BasePaginator.default_error_messages`, the messages that `BasePaginator._validate_number` raises with (`django/core/paginator.py:BasePaginator.__init__`).
`AsyncPaginator` and `AsyncPage` came in 6.0, and what `AsyncPaginator` shares with `Paginator` is in their base class, `BasePaginator` (`django/core/paginator.py:BasePaginator`).

`AsyncPage` is not a sequence: its length and indexes raise `TypeError` while its objects are not a list, until `AsyncPage.aget_object_list` makes them one (`django/core/paginator.py:AsyncPage`; [Pagination: `Paginator` and `Page`](../services/pagination.md#asyncpaginator-and-asyncpage)).

Since 6.0 `BasePaginator.__init__` warns with `RemovedInDjango2028Warning` when the orphans are not fewer than the page size, and a comment there gives the `ValueError` it is to raise in Django 2028 (`django/core/paginator.py:BasePaginator.__init__`; [What still warns: the deprecations and the releases that end them](deprecations.md)).
